definitions: To hold onto something tightly, often to avoid falling or losing it.
To maintain a strong emotional or physical attachment to someone or something.
To try to keep something, such as hope, an idea, or a possession, often despite difficulties.
examples: She had to cling on to the railing to avoid slipping.
He continues to cling on to the hope of winning the lottery.
They tried to cling on to their old traditions.
The child would cling on to her mother's hand in the crowd.
pastTenses: clung on to, clung on to
